English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
fita
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian фита́ (fitá).

Noun

[edit]

fita (plural fitas)

  1. The obsolete Cyrillic letter Ѳ, ѳ formerly used in Russian to write proper names and loanwords derived from or via Greek.

Translations

[edit]
Ѳ
  • French: fita (fr) f, phita f
  • Russian: фита́ (ru) f (fitá), ѳита́ f (fitá) (pre-1918 reform spelling)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • fiat, IATF, Fiat, FIAT, Taif, Tafi, Fait, fait

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *[petra] fīcta, from Latin petra (“stone”) and figere (“to fix in place”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈfi.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈfi.ta]
  • Audio (Catalonia):(file)

Noun

[edit]

fita f (plural fites)

  1. milestone, boundary stone
    Synonym: molló
  2. waypoint
  3. (mathematics) bound
Derived terms
[edit]
  • fita inferior
  • fita superior
  • fitar
Related terms
[edit]
  • fit

Further reading

[edit]
  • “fita”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “fita”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “fita” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “fita” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

fita

  1. inflection of fitar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Franco-Provençal

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈfita] (Aosta)

Noun

[edit]

fita (Valdôtain, Vaudois)

  1. alternative form of féta (“party, celebration”)

References

[edit]
  • fête in Patois VdA: Le site du Francoprovençal en Vallée d'Aoste – on patoisvda.org
  • Walther von Wartburg (1928–2002), “fĕsta”, in Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch, volume 3: D–F, page 482

Galician

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfita/ [ˈfi.t̪ɐ]
  • Rhymes: -ita
  • Hyphenation: fi‧ta

Etymology 1

[edit]

Probably from Latin vitta (“ribbon”), although the required evolution, with Latin <vi> becoming /fi/, is irregular. Alternatively from Suevic, from a derivative of Proto-Germanic *fetjō, compare Old High German fizza (“thread, tissue”), Old Norse fitja (“to knit”).[1] Compare also Italian fetta.

Noun

[edit]

fita f (plural fitas)

  1. band, ribbon
  2. (sewing) wristband, girdle, hem
  3. elongated plot of land

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin fictum (“fixed”).

Adjective

[edit]

fita

  1. feminine singular of fito
Derived terms
[edit]
  • Pedrafita

Verb

[edit]

fita

  1. inflection of fitar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “fita”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “fita”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “fita”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

Macanese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese fita.

Noun

[edit]

fita (plural fita-fita)

  1. tape, ribbon, band
    fita di sapato ― shoelaces (literally, “shoe ribbon”)
  2. film, movie
    Synonym: pintura
    fita-cinéma ― film
    olâ fita ― to see a movie, to go to the cinema

Derived terms

[edit]
  • fazê-fita (“to be duplicitous”)

References

[edit]
  • https://www.macaneselibrary.org/pub/english/uipatua.htm#f

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfi.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfi.tɐ/

  • Rhymes: -itɐ
  • Hyphenation: fi‧ta

Etymology 1

[edit]

Uncertain. Likely from Latin vitta (“band, ribbon”).

Noun

[edit]

fita f (plural fitas)

  1. tape, ribbon, band
  2. (colloquial) film, movie
    Synonyms: filme, película
  3. (Brazil, video games, colloquial) cartridge
    Synonym: cartucho
  4. (Portugal, education, slang) a colored ribbon to indicate membership of a faculty
  5. (Portugal, colloquial) necktie
    Synonym: gravata

[edit]

For quotations using this term, see Citations:fita.

[edit]

  • → Konkani: फीत (phīt)
  • → Marathi: फीत (phīt)

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin ficta.

Noun

[edit]

fita f (plural fitas)

  1. act, deception, lie
    É tudo fita!
    It's all an act!
    Deixem-se de fitas!
    Stop pretending!
  2. tantrum
    Fazer fita.
    To pull a tantrum.
